The requests' targets: `(i%2)<<80` puts the lease index in bits 80-95, i.e., '2001:db8:0:X::...' where X = i%2 → 2001:db8:0:0.. wait: bits 80-95 correspond to the third group (hextet 2: bits 96-111) and fourth group (hextet 3: bits 80-95). So the address is 2001:db8:0:(i%2)::iid. And the lease prefix is '2001:db8:%x::/56' % i → 2001:db8:0::/56 and 2001:db8:1::/56. Hmm, for lease L1 = 2001:db8:1::/56, the target should be within 2001:db8:1:0000-00ff... My constructed address has hextet2=0 and hextet3=i%2, so for lease 1 the address 2001:db8:0:1::... is NOT in 2001:db8:1::/56. But that doesn't matter for the plan (no requirement that the request target is in the lease). What matters is the offer prefix containment.

Offers: prefix /32 (2001:db8::/32) contains everything ✓, or /56, /64 random.

So why only 2 assignments? Ah — the request quota forest: capacity of nodes... The path from a request's group to the root must have capacity ≥1 at every node.
